title: Deferred admission crediting and grace-levels for tenant priority
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a deferred admission crediting system paired with configurable grace-levels to improve tenant experience during transient overload and multi-region failover. The mechanism awards credits to tenants during steady-state or under-utilized periods; credits may be spent to bypass strict admission limits when short spikes occur. Credits decay over time and are subject to per-tenant maxima. The feature integrates with the existing admission controller and circuit-breaker layer to enable staged degradation: (1) soft-accept using credits, (2) graceful fidelity reduction (shorten response length, lower sampling temperature, use cached prefixes), and (3) fallback to pre-defined model variants when available. The ticket covers design, runtime implementation, config surface, telemetry, and a small console UI for ops to inspect credit balances and grace-levels across regions.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Observability and Runtime teams
Admission controller accepts a credit-backed request path that consumes a tenant credit and is measurable in tracing
Credit issuance policy is configurable per-tenant and per-region with sensible defaults
Credits decay policy implemented and documented (half-life, max bucket size)
When credits are exhausted, admission falls back to configured degradation ladder reliably
Circuit breaker events trigger an emergency grace-level that reduces credit issuance within 60s
End-to-end tests simulate sustained spike and verify SLO breach rate reduces by >=15% for top 10 tenants using credits
Console shows balances and audit events for credit spending and issuance
Monitoring: dashboards with credit burn rate, regional reconciliation errors, and alerting thresholds
notes: Motivation: current blunt admission policies either reject or heavily degrade requests causing poor UX for premium tenants during short spikes. Credits provide a predictable way to offer short-lived leniency tied to tenant SLAs.

Trade-offs: credits add state and reconciliation complexity for multi-region operation. We prefer eventual consistency with bounded reconciliation rather than synchronously replicated counters to avoid latency amplification.

Design decision: use local per-region credit pools with periodic reconciliation and negative-correction on conflict. This keeps fast-path admission local and avoids cross-region RPCs on every request.
Fallback ladder: (1) credit-backed accept -> (2) truncated response mode -> (3) cached-prefix replay -> (4) cheaper model variant -> (5) hard reject. Each step must be observable and reversible.
Telemetry requirements captured: span tags for credit_used=true/false, credit_balance after request, grace_level applied, and circuit_breaker_state.
Performance targets: credit check/consume should add <0.6ms p50 and <2ms p99 to request latency in our Java admission path.
implementation_tasks: Design doc: detailed sequence diagrams and reconciliation plan
Runtime: extend admission controller with local credit buckets and non-blocking consume API
Persistence: lightweight event-sourced ledger for credits with region-tagged checkpoints
Circuit breaker integration: when a breaker trips, reduce issuance rate by configured factor
Degradation ladder: implement short-circuit hooks to trigger fidelity reductions downstream
Observability: traces, metrics, dashboards and SLO-linked alerts
Console: read-only view for ops + ability to grant emergency credits via runbook
E2E tests: unit, integration with multi-region simulation, and load tests
risks: State divergence across regions could temporarily over-commit credits leading to unfair usage
Complexity of replayable credit ledger under high write load
Incorrectly tuned grace-levels may hide SLO regressions instead of preventing them
Edge cases around billing: need to ensure credit-backed accepts are accounted against usage billing
mitigations: Bounded overcommit: allow a small configurable overcommit factor and fast reconciliation with corrective throttles
Backpressure: throttle credit issuance if ledger write latency rises above safe threshold
Observability: add dedicated SLOs for credit system health and reconciliation lag
Billing: emit audit events that tie credit usage to tenant billing pipeline; billing team to validate mapping before GA
